nodes.description: Some carriers have a small cornea, iris coloboma or, in the translocation family, anterior segment dysgenesis with corneal opacity and microphthalmia. nodes.description: Lens extraction for visually significant cataract, from infancy for dense congenital opacities (lensectomy and anterior vitrectomy at 7-8 weeks with aphakic contact lenses in the K308E patient; extraction with posterior chamber intraocular lens at 4 years for Y301H). For dense bilateral congenital cataract the timing of surgery in the first weeks governs visual outcome; that evidence comes from cohorts not genotyped for MAF. No MAF-directed therapy exists.

nodes.description: MAF is strongly induced at the lens equator, where epithelial cells leave the cell cycle and become fiber cells. Without MAF, posterior lens cells fail to elongate, keep synthesizing DNA and do not express alpha-A and beta-crystallins; deleting Maf in adult mice also disrupts fiber cell differentiation and lens structure.

nodes.description: A dominant DNA-binding-domain allele giving mild pulverulent cataract in heterozygotes, and anterior segment abnormalities on another genetic background.

Heterozygous germline MAF alleles, nearly all missense changes at conserved residues of the C-terminal DNA-binding domain: the extended homology region (V271E), the basic region (R288P, K297R, R299S, Y301H, Gln303) and the leucine zipper and its flank (K308E, L316P). One family carries a t(5;16)(p15.3;q23.2) translocation whose 16q23.2 breakpoint transects the MAF genomic-control domain, and one family carries an N-terminal frameshift (c.177dup). How each allele changes MAF function differs (see the downstream nodes and the dominance discussion).
